paragraphs.en: The council meeting dragged on until one pirate re-entered the house, asking for a torch with an ironic salute. Silver agreed briefly, and the man left again.
paragraphs.zh: 会议一直拖到一个海盗重新进入房子，带着讽刺的敬礼要了一根火把。银勉强答应了，那人随后离开了。

paragraphs.en: Silver then said, "There's a breeze coming, Jim," adopting a friendly tone.
paragraphs.zh: 银色随后说道：“吉姆，有微风吹来了,”他采用了友好的语气。

paragraphs.en: I turned to the nearest loophole and saw that the embers of the fire had dimmed significantly. The pirates needed light; they were gathered halfway down the slope towards the stockade. One held a torch while another knelt, his knife blade glinting in moonlight and torchlight.
paragraphs.zh: 我转向最近的一个缺口，发现篝火的余烬已经暗淡了不少。海盗们需要光源；他们聚集在木栅栏下方约一半的位置。其中一个拿着火炬，另一个则跪在地上，月光和火光照耀下，他的刀刃闪烁着寒光。

paragraphs.en: The rest watched intently.
paragraphs.zh: 其余的人都聚精会神地注视着。

paragraphs.en: The kneeling man stood up, and the group moved towards the house. "Here they come," I said, returning to my position.
paragraphs.zh: 跪着的人站了起来，众人朝房子走去。“他们来了，”我回到原位说道。

paragraphs.en: Silver replied cheerfully, "Let 'em come, lad—let 'em come. I still have a shot left."
paragraphs.zh: 银色回答道，满是自信：“让他们来吧，伙计——让他们来。我还有最后一击的机会。”

paragraphs.en: The door opened, and five pirates huddled inside pushed one forward. He hesitated as he stepped, holding his right hand out in front of him.
paragraphs.zh: 门开了，五个海盗挤在门口，推了一个出来。那人犹豫了一下，迈步上前时，右手伸在身前。

paragraphs.en: "Step up," Silver called. "I won't eat you. Hand it over, lubber.
paragraphs.zh: “快点上来，”银叫道，“我不会吃你的。把东西给我，大块头。”

paragraphs.en: I know the rules; I won't hurt a depytation."
paragraphs.zh: 我知道游戏规则；我不会伤害一个对手。

paragraphs.en: Encouraged by this, the pirate stepped forward and passed something to Silver, slipping back quickly to his companions.
paragraphs.zh: 受到这一鼓励，海盗迈前一步，把什么东西递给了锡尔弗，然后迅速退回，重新加入了同伴的行列。

paragraphs.en: Silver examined what was given. "The black spot! I thought so," he said.
paragraphs.zh: 银色仔细检查了手中的东西。“那个黑点！我就知道会有这么一天。”他脱口而出。

paragraphs.en: "Where did you get that paper? Look here, now; this ain't lucky! You've cut it out of a Bible.
paragraphs.zh: “你从哪儿弄来这张纸？你看好了，这可不吉利！你这是从圣经上裁下来的。”

paragraphs.en: What fool's cut a Bible?"
paragraphs.zh: 谁这么蠢把圣经给割裂了？

paragraphs.en: Morgan chimed in, "Ah, there! There! Wot did I say?
paragraphs.zh: 摩根插嘴道：“啊，就是那儿！那儿！我说对了吧？”

paragraphs.en: No good'll come o' that."
paragraphs.zh: 那可不行。

paragraphs.en: Silver continued, "Well, you've about fixed it now, among you. You'll all swing now, I reckon. What soft-headed lubber had a Bible?"
paragraphs.zh: Silver 继续说道：“好了，现在你们自己搞定了。你们几个都得吃点苦头了，我想。是谁这个头脑简单的家伙拿走了圣经？”

paragraphs.en: Dick was identified as the culprit.
paragraphs.zh: 狄克被认作是罪犯。

paragraphs.en: "Let Dick handle his prayers," said Silver. "He’s had his share of luck, and you can count on that."
paragraphs.zh: “让迪克去祈祷吧，”锡尔弗说道，“他运气不错，你得指望上这一点。”

paragraphs.en: But the long man with yellow eyes interrupted.
paragraphs.zh: 但那双黄眼睛的高个子男子插嘴道。

paragraphs.en: "Belay that talk, John Silver," he commanded. "The crew has given you the black spot in full council. Turn it over and see what's written there before you speak."
paragraphs.zh: “住口，约翰·辛格尔,”他命令道，“船员们在全体会议上已经给你发放了黑点。在开口说话之前，先看看上面写了什么。”

paragraphs.en: "Thank you, George," replied the sea-cook. "You're always quick on business and know the rules well. So, what is it?
paragraphs.zh: “谢谢，乔治，”海厨回答道，“你总是精明能干，对规则也很熟悉。那么，出什么事了？”

paragraphs.en: 'Deposed,' that’s your message, isn't it? Your handwriting, George? You were becoming quite a leader here.
paragraphs.zh: “罢免令，”这不就是你的意思吗？乔治，你的笔迹？你在这里可真成了一个领导者了。

paragraphs.en: Next captain, I wouldn’t be surprised. Just give me back that torch, will you? This pipe doesn't draw."
paragraphs.zh: 下一任船长我也不会感到意外。你把那支火炬还给我行不行？这烟斗抽不着火。

paragraphs.en: "Come now," said George. "You're not fooling this crew anymore. You’re a funny man, but your time is up.
paragraphs.zh: “好了，”乔治说道，“别再蒙我们了。你虽然风趣，但好景不长了。”

paragraphs.en: Step down from the barrel and help vote."
paragraphs.zh: 下来帮忙投票吧。

paragraphs.en: Silver retorted contemptuously, "If you know the rules, say so. Otherwise, I do, and I'll wait here until you present your complaints. Your black spot isn't worth a biscuit in the meantime.
paragraphs.zh: 银色不屑一顾地反问道：“如果你知道规则，就直说。否则，我知道这些规则，我会在这里等着你提出你的抱怨。在这之前，你的黑点连一块饼干都换不来。”

paragraphs.en: After that, we’ll see."
paragraphs.zh: 之后我们就见分晓了。

paragraphs.en: "Enough," replied George. "We're all square. First, you've messed up this cruise—dare to deny it?
paragraphs.zh: “够了，”乔治说道，“我们扯平了。首先，你搞砸了这次航行——敢不承认吗？

paragraphs.en: Second, you let the enemy escape for nothing. Why did they want out? Third, you wouldn’t attack them on the march.
paragraphs.zh: 其次，你让敌人白白逃走了。他们为什么要逃跑呢？再者，你在行军途中没有攻击他们。

paragraphs.en: We see through you, John Silver; you want to play booty. And fourth, there’s this boy."
paragraphs.zh: 我们看穿你了，约翰·辛内尔；你想来一手。还有一点，就是这个孩子。

paragraphs.en: Silver paused, and George Merry's face showed he had been deeply moved by Silver’s words.
paragraphs.zh: 赛勒斯顿了顿，乔治·梅里脸上流露出他被赛勒斯的话深深触动的表情。

paragraphs.en: "Number one answered!" cried Merry, wiping sweat from his brow. He had spoken with such intensity that it shook the room.
paragraphs.zh: 梅里喊道：“一号回答！”说着他擦去了额头上的汗珠，语气之强烈竟让整个房间都为之震动。

paragraphs.en: "You've no sense or memory," Silver continued. "I leave it to your mothers where you came to sea. Sea!
paragraphs.zh: “你既没有理智也没有记忆，”西尔弗接着说，“你们的出身让你们的母亲去解释吧。大海！

paragraphs.en: Gentlemen of fortune? You're tailors."
paragraphs.zh: 你们这些有钱人？你们倒是裁缝啊。

paragraphs.en: Morgan urged, "Go on, John. Speak up to the others."
paragraphs.zh: 摩根催促道：“约翰，快点，对其他人说吧。”

paragraphs.en: John returned to his point: "Ah, the others! They're a fine bunch. You say this cruise is a mess?
paragraphs.zh: 约翰又回到了正题：“啊，其他人！他们可是一流的"group。你认为这次巡游一团糟？”

paragraphs.en: Well, if you knew how badly bungled it was, you'd see! We’re so close to disaster that my neck feels stiff just thinking about it. Imagine seeing them hanged in chains, with birds circling and sailors pointing at them as they go down with the tide.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你知道这计划糟糕到了什么程度，你就会明白了！我们离灾难已经近在咫尺，光是想想都觉得脊背发凉。想象一下他们被锁链捆绑着吊死，鸟儿盘旋在上空，水手们指指点点地看着他们随潮水一同沉没，那情景真是令人不寒而栗。

paragraphs.en: 'Who’s that?' one asks, and another replies, 'That's John Silver; I knew him well.' The chains jangle as you move to reach for the next buoy.
paragraphs.zh: “是谁？”一个人问道，另一个人回答：“那是约翰·赛维尔；我跟他挺熟的。”你移动身体去够下一个浮标时，手链发出叮当作响的声音。

paragraphs.en: That’s where we are, thanks to Silver, Hands, Anderson, and other fools like them.
paragraphs.zh: 正因为Silver、Hands、Anderson以及其他这些蠢货，我们才到了这个地步。

paragraphs.en: If you want to know about number four and the boy, he’s a hostage. We won’t waste a hostage, will we? He might be our last chance, and I wouldn't doubt it.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你想知道四号人物和那个男孩的情况，他是个人质。我们不会浪费一个人质的，对吧？他可能是我们的最后机会，我可不信他会让我们失望。

paragraphs.en: Kill that boy? Not me, mates! And what about number three?
paragraphs.zh: 杀那个男孩？可不是我干的！还有第三号呢？

paragraphs.en: There's much to say there. Maybe you didn't realize a consort was coming—John with his broken head or George Merry with ague just six hours ago, still looking like lemon peel. But the consort is here and soon; we'll see who wants a hostage then.
paragraphs.zh: 那里有很多事情要说。或许你没有意识到会有王伴侣来访——比如约翰刚刚脑部受伤，或是乔治·梅里才发高烧六个小时，现在还面色苍白如同柠檬皮。但王伴侣已经到了，而且很快就会正式登门；到时候看看谁还想抓个人质吧。

paragraphs.en: As for number two, why I made that bargain? You came crawling on your knees to me, so downhearted you might have starved if not for me—still, it’s a small matter! Look there—that's why!"
paragraphs.zh: 至于第二件事，我为什么要做出那样的交易呢？你跪着爬到我面前，心灰意冷几乎饿死——但这也算不了什么！你看那边，那就是原因！

paragraphs.en: He tossed a paper onto the floor. It was the chart from the captain's chest, yellow with three red crosses. I recognized it instantly.
paragraphs.zh: 他把一张纸扔在地上。那是一张从船长胸膛取出的图表，黄色的纸上用红笔标了三个叉。我一眼就认了出来。

paragraphs.en: The doctor had given it to him, but why, I couldn’t imagine.
paragraphs.zh: 医生给了他这个药，但我实在想不出原因。

paragraphs.en: The surviving mutineers were stunned by its appearance. They leaped upon it like cats on a mouse, tearing it from hand to hand. Oaths and cries filled the air as they examined it, their childish laughter suggesting they were handling gold itself or already at sea with it in safety.
paragraphs.zh: 幸存的叛乱者们对它的出现感到震惊，如同猫捕鼠般扑了上去，你推我搡地争夺着。咒骂和喊声此起彼伏，他们仔细检查着这一切，稚嫩的笑声仿佛手中握的是真正的黄金，或是已经带着它安全出海。

paragraphs.en: Silver suddenly stood up, leaning against the wall. "George," he warned, "if you say another word, I'll call you down and fight you."
paragraphs.zh: 银突然站起身来，倚在墙上。“乔治，”他警告道，“如果你再啰唆一句，我就把你叫下来和你决斗。”

paragraphs.en: "Fair enough," agreed Morgan.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧,”摩根同意道。

paragraphs.en: "Fair!" Silver retorted. "You lost the ship; I found the treasure.
paragraphs.zh: “公平！”银色反驳道，“你失去了船只，我找到了财宝。”

paragraphs.en: Who's better at that? I resign now. Elect your captain, if you like."
paragraphs.zh: 谁比我还擅长这个？我辞职了。你们要是愿意，就选个船长吧。

paragraphs.en: "Silver!" they shouted. "Barbecue forever!
paragraphs.zh: “银狐！”他们喊道，“烧烤万岁！”

paragraphs.en: Barbecue for captain!"
paragraphs.zh: “为船长烧烤！”

paragraphs.en: Silver continued, "The black spot isn't much good now. Dick has spoiled his Bible."
paragraphs.zh: Silver 继续说道：“那个黑点现在已经没多大用了。迪克把他的圣经弄坏了。”

paragraphs.en: Dick grumbled, uneasy about the curse he had brought upon himself.
paragraphs.zh: 迪克嘟囔着嘴，对自己招来的厄运感到不安。

paragraphs.en: Silver tossed me a piece of paper. It was roughly the size of a crown piece, one side blank and the other with a verse from Revelation: "Without are dogs and murderers." The printed side was blackened with ash, which was already smudging my fingers.
paragraphs.zh: 银色递给我一张纸，大约和一枚金币大小相当，一面空白，另一面则印着启示录中的一段经文：“门外有狗和杀人犯。”印刷的一面已经熏黑了，灰烬还沾染在我的手指上。

paragraphs.en: On the back, written in the same material, was the single word "Depposed."
paragraphs.zh: 背面用同样的材料写着一个单词：“废黜”。

paragraphs.en: Silver kept the paper beside him; now there was no trace of writing left except for a faint scratch.
paragraphs.zh: 赛勒斯依旧把那张纸放在身边；现在除了淡淡的划痕外，上面已没有任何书写痕迹。

paragraphs.en: The night's business concluded, we retired with a round of drinks before settling down to sleep. Silver assigned George Merry to watch over us and warned him severely about any failure.
paragraphs.zh: 夜幕下的交易告一段落后，我们先小酌了几杯才上床休息。赛勒斯指派乔治·梅里守夜，并对他进行了严厉的警告，叮嘱他不可有丝毫疏忽。

paragraphs.en: I struggled to fall asleep, consumed by thoughts of the man I had killed earlier that day and my precarious position. The most pressing concern was Silver’s desperate scheme to keep the mutineers united while desperately trying to secure his own survival.
paragraphs.zh: 我辗转反侧，脑海中不断回荡着当天早些时候杀人的场景以及自己岌岌可危的处境。最让人焦虑的是，Silver那条垂死挣扎的计策——既要极力维系叛乱者的团结，又要拼命确保自己的生存。

paragraphs.en: Despite his wickedness, I felt a pang for Silver, who slept soundly but faced grave dangers and a humiliating fate.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管塞维尔的所作所为令人不齿，我还是为他感到一丝担忧。他睡得正香，却面临着巨大的危险和屈辱的命运。
